caption:
A $5,000-a-month assistant versus a $200-a-month agent. The comparison gets posted a lot. It's also the wrong comparison.

The cost side is real. In the US, the median executive secretary or executive administrative assistant earns about $75,000 a year — roughly $6,300 a month before payroll taxes, equipment and paid time off (US Bureau of Labor Statistics). An agent running the same repetitive tasks costs a fraction of that.

But the two aren't buying you the same thing.

A person brings judgment: reading a situation you didn't describe in advance, noticing that a request is odd, deciding what matters this week. That doesn't automate, and it shouldn't.

An agent brings repetition without fatigue: the same check, the same follow-up, the same handoff, at 2am, on the four-hundredth run, exactly as on the first.

So the honest question isn't "person or agent". It's how much of the person's week is currently spent on the part that never needed judgment in the first place.

What's the most repetitive hour in your week right now?
